course_name_original: Integración ambiental de proyectos de ingeniería

learning_outcomes.text: Participate in the environmental impact assessment process of an engineering project.
Perform the search and analysis of necessary information to carry out the study of the environment where the project will be installed.
Identify main impacts and propose and dimension corrective measures in the most common types of engineering projects.
Evaluate the need to apply technologies corresponding to BATs (Best Available Techniques) to a specific project, as well as be able to identify the necessary BAT for a given project.
Draft and process an Integrated Environmental Authorization.
Understand the flexibility mechanisms of the Kyoto Protocol (clean development mechanisms, joint implementation initiatives, and emissions trading).

syllabus_topics: Conceptual framework of environmental impact assessment.
Legal framework of environmental impact assessment.
Environmental impact assessment on the atmosphere.
Environmental impact assessment on hydrology and hydrogeology.
Environmental impact assessment on soil, geology, and geomorphology.
Environmental impact assessment on the landscape.
Environmental impact assessment on the socioeconomic environment and cultural resources.
Environmental impact assessment on historical-artistic heritage.
Integrated pollution control and prevention: Best Available Techniques (BATs), Emission Limit Values, and Integrated Environmental Authorization.
Drafting an 'Environmental Impact Study': Search and analysis of information for the study of the environment where the project will be installed.
Drafting an 'Environmental Impact Study': Identification of main impacts and proposal/dimensioning of necessary corrective measures.
Drafting an 'Environmental Impact Study': Establishment of an environmental monitoring program.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, it is necessary to obtain a grade equal to or greater than 50% of the total score for written tests, as well as a grade equal to or greater than 50% of the total score for the proposed work (which integrates practice reports and projects). If this critical evaluation criterion is not met, the final grade for the course will be FAIL, with the resulting score from the sum of all obtained assessment scores, truncated to a maximum of 4.5 points. For students recognized with part-time dedication, non-recoverable activities may be replaced by similar activities with different deadlines or equivalent assessment tests.
